title: John Chrysostom on 2 Timothy 1:1
body: “What is the reason of his writing this second Epistle to Timothy? He had said, "I hope to come unto thee shortly" (1 Tim.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 1
bodyEs: “¿Cuál es la razón de que escriba esta segunda epístola a Timoteo? Había dicho: «iré presto á ti» (1 Tim.”

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Timothy 1:8
body: “There is nothing worse than that man should measure and judge of divine things by human reasonings. For thus he will fall from that rock a vast distance, and be deprived of the light.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 2
bodyEs: “No hay nada peor que el que el hombre mida y juzgue las cosas divinas por razonamientos humanos. Porque así caerá de aquella roca una distancia inmensa, y será privado de la luz.”

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Timothy 1:13
body: “Not by letters alone did Paul instruct his disciple in his duty, but before by words also which he shows, both in many other passages, as where he says, "whether by word or our Epistle" (2 Thess.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 3
bodyEs: “No solo por cartas instruyó Pablo a su discípulo en su deber, sino antes también por palabras, lo cual muestra, tanto en muchos otros pasajes, como donde dice: «sea por palabra, ó por carta nuestra» (2 Tes.”

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Timothy 2:1
body: “The young sailor at sea is inspired with great confidence, if the Master of the ship has been preserved in a shipwreck. For he will not consider that it is from his inexperience that he is exposed to the storm, but from the nature of things; and this has no little effect upon his mind.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 4
bodyEs: “El joven marinero en el mar se llena de gran confianza si el capitán del barco se ha salvado en un naufragio. Porque no pensará que es por su inexperiencia que está expuesto a la tormenta, sino por la naturaleza de las cosas; y esto no tiene poco efecto sobre su mente.”

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Timothy 2:11
body: “Many of the weaker sort of men give up the effort of faith, and do not endure the deferring of their hope. They seek things present, and form from these their judgment of the future.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 5
bodyEs: “Muchos de los hombres más débiles abandonan el esfuerzo de la fe, y no soportan el diferir de su esperanza. Buscan las cosas presentes, y por estas forman su juicio del futuro.”

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Timothy 2:20
body: “Many men are still even now perplexed to account for the fact, that the wicked are suffered to remain, and are not yet destroyed. Now doubtless various reasons may be assigned for this, as, that they may be converted, or that by their punishment they may be made an example to the multitude.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 6
bodyEs: “Muchos hombres todavía aun ahora están perplejos para explicar el hecho de que se permita que los malos permanezcan, y que todavía no sean destruidos. Ahora bien, sin duda pueden darse varias razones de esto, como que puedan convertirse, o que por su castigo se hagan ejemplo para la multitud.”

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Timothy 3:1
body: “He had said in the former Epistle, that "the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith" (1 Tim.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 7
bodyEs: “Había dicho en la epístola anterior que «el Espíritu dice manifiestamente, que en los venideros tiempos algunos apostatarán de la fe» (1 Tim.”

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Timothy 3:1
body: “If any now takes offense at the existence of heretics, let him remember that it was so from the beginning, the devil always setting up error by the side of truth. God from the beginning promised good, the devil came too with a promise.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 8
bodyEs: “Si alguno se ofende ahora de que existan herejes, recuerde que así fue desde el principio, poniendo el diablo siempre el error al lado de la verdad. Dios desde el principio prometió el bien, y el diablo vino también con una promesa.”

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Timothy 3:16
body: “Having offered much exhortation and consolation from other sources, he adds that which is more perfect, derived from the Scriptures; and he is reasonably full in offering consolation, because he has a great and sad thing to say.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 9
bodyEs: “Habiendo ofrecido mucha exhortación y consuelo de otras fuentes, añade lo que es más perfecto, derivado de las Escrituras; y está razonablemente lleno al ofrecer consuelo, porque tiene algo grande y triste que decir.”

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Timothy 4:9
body: “It is worth while to enquire why he calls Timothy to him, inasmuch as he was intrusted with a Church, and a whole nation. It was not from arrogance.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon, Homily 10
bodyEs: “Vale la pena preguntar por qué llama a Timoteo a sí, puesto que se le había confiado una Iglesia y toda una nación. No era por arrogancia.”
